contract_changes_needed: pnpm-lock.yaml (L0): needs importers for packages/net and apps/server. Installed here with pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile, which is what CI uses; the lockfile is left modified in the working tree and deliberately not committed because L0 owns it. CI will fail on --frozen-lockfile until L0 regenerates it.

scripts/wire-deps.cjs (L0): its project graph does not know the two new workspace projects, so the workspace:* dependencies in packages/net/package.json and apps/server/package.json were written by hand. No root package.json edit was needed.
packages/core-types/src/v2/net.ts: no change needed. Every opcode, constant, kick reason, header layout and interface was used exactly as frozen.
notes: packages/net (@voxelcraft/net): byte reader/writer, 8 byte frame codec with a streaming FrameSplitter, encoders and decoders for all 14 opcodes, 28 byte entity snapshot records, chunk payload reuse of the frozen save codec, INPUT_BIT helpers, protocol compatibility guards, heartbeat bookkeeping, a client connection state machine with capped exponential reconnect, a server session registry, and an RFC 6455 websocket implementation (handshake, masking, fragmentation, close codes) on node:http and node:crypto.

apps/server (@voxelcraft/server): authoritative world store and generator, block edit validation against reach and block ids, movement clamping, 20 Hz tick loop with 10 Hz snapshots, time sync every 5 s, block change broadcast, per client chunk streaming, heartbeat timeouts and the frozen kick reasons for protocol mismatch, server full, timeout and bad message. Single endpoint /ws, default port 8787, overridable by PORT.
No new npm dependency was added. Node 22's global WebSocket is used as the test client.

Chunk streaming: square radius 6 (169 columns, corners included), nearest first with a cx then cz tie break, token bucket averaging 24 columns per second per client with a 12 column burst cap. startGameServer and createGameServer inject this streamer by default, so a production boot streams; GameServer itself still streams nothing unless handed a queue, which keeps its unit tests policy free.

decodeChunkPayload returns cx 0 and cz 0 by design: the payload is byte for byte the save codec and carries no coordinates. The ChunkData frame header is the source of truth, and callers must take cx and cz from there.

The headless integration test starts the server on port 0, connects two real websocket clients, completes hello and welcome with distinct player ids, has one client edit a block and asserts the other receives the BlockChange, and asserts streamed ChunkData round trips through the chunk codec. No fixed port is ever bound.

Work was split across three L2 children: protocol codec plus tests, authoritative world store plus validation, and chunk streaming plus the integration test. All three reported green and every line was re-verified and committed by L1-E; the frame codec, transport, protocol guards, heartbeat, sessions, tick loop, movement, game server, boot path and default streamer wiring were implemented by L1-E directly.
The Playwright suite was not run, as agreed in the brief.
